_comment: THE SHARED STAGE LIBRARY — what more than one scene's `surface` nodes draw from. Today that is the `lighting` presets (studio / night / deep_space) every stage NAMES; a stage source that only one scene uses is that scene's data and lives in its .scene.json `stages` section (ruling 8DE71FB0, 2026-08-22). A source says WHAT to render (lighting preset, clear, camera, content layers); the NODE says WHERE it lands. Draw ORDER is derived topologically by flicker-render::FrameGraph, never expressed here. Layers carry scalars and $token colours — never geometry. Colours are $token refs resolved against ui_theme.json's theme.tokens at load (the loader merges this file into the theme root, then each scene's `stages` INTO this block — a scene stage may not reuse a library name; the palette NEVER lives here; a `theme` key in this file is refused as a fork). Every source is compiled by the ONE stage compiler (flicker-widgets stages.rs): an unknown key, draw kind or preset fails the build gate `every_shipped_stage_compiles_clean`. The `lighting` presets are salvaged from the retired packeditor (pip_scene / night_scene).

deep_space._comment: ONE STAR, lit from where it actually is: the Solar Birth cinematic's system is shaded by a POINT light at the world origin (`point_pos` + `point`, a warm starlight), so every body takes its terminator from its own direction to the centre — which is the only way a fly-through of a fixed system reads as lit rather than as a flat directional wash. The directional sun and moon are therefore BLACK, and their `*_dir` are inert (kept so the rig states every term rather than leaving three to a default nobody chose). `ambient` is a faint floor that keeps night sides off pure black, and the sky palette is a near-black deep space — the `sky` pass of `solarbirth_sky` rides it.

hearth._comment: THE FIREPLACE-CLASS RIG — the first shipped preset whose light has real FALLOFF and a DRIVER, authored for the Prism Test Room's root surface (`pocclusters_world` in pocclusters.scene.json) and for nothing else. It is the general `lights` form, and the SLOT ORDER is load-bearing: the Celestial Cycle composes over this rig every frame (`CelestialState::over`, flicker-pocclusters/src/celestial.rs) and overwrites lights 0 and 1 BY INDEX — the sun and the moon — together with `ambient`, the sky palette and the fog. Those same two slots are what the sky pass reads back (`sky_sun()`/`sky_moon()` ARE slots 0/1, one addressing scheme), so a non-`dir` light authored into either is REPORTED by the preset compiler rather than silently eaten — fixed lights belong at slot 2+. Those two slots are therefore RESERVED, not lit: their colour is black and their `dir` points below the horizon (the deep_space idiom — inert, but stated, so the rig names every term rather than leaving it to a default nobody chose). Black is the honest placeholder: a studio-ish sun here would be a light nobody authored for this room, seen only if the compose path were bypassed — and in that case a dark sky is the failure worth seeing. `ambient` / `sky_zenith` / `sky_horizon` / fog are deliberately UNAUTHORED for the same reason the scene's `ground_fog` authors no `density`: the cycle owns them, so a number here would be dead data. Slot 2 is the hearth itself.

lights._comment: SLOT 0 — the sun. Reserved by index; the Celestial Cycle overwrites colour AND direction every frame.
SLOT 1 — the moon. Reserved by index, same as slot 0.

THE HEARTH — every number here is ART, Aaron's to tune in THIS file, never in Rust. `color` is firelight HUE only (a warm orange); the magnitude rides `intensity`. `pos` is world VOXELS in the 3×3 field of 256-voxel clusters (bounds 0..768): the player spawns at the field centre (384, 384) facing +Z, so the fire sits 20 voxels ahead of that walk line and 4 to the right of it, and y=120 is ~3 voxels above the terrain there (the world heightmap reads ~116.7 at 388/404) — on the nav floor and in the spawn view, neither buried nor floating. `intensity` 36 is in the TENS on purpose: a light with a `radius` takes true windowed inverse-square falloff, the one place the engine's colour-carries-the-magnitude convention stops holding — at 36 the pool reads about half of albedo some 8 voxels out and is gone at 16. `radius` 16 voxels IS that edge (~2.3 m at this scene's 12-voxel eye height). The `driver` is seeded value noise that only ever DIMS a fire and never overshoots it, evaluated once per frame by FrameGraph::surface against the clock this scene publishes: `speed` 7 noise samples a second, `depth` 0.35 = at most a 35% cut, `seed` 1 so a second fire in this room can differ by its seed alone.
